value.content:
Resizing the dish photo is a task: a worker does it once and it's done, a queue. RabbitMQ's queue is built to empty out; Amazon SQS runs on AWS, scales without provisioning and keeps messages for up to 14 days. The "order paid" event is history: several services read at their own pace and can re-read, a log, Kafka. And the line has blurred: RabbitMQ has streams, and Kafka has share groups.

Which of the three do you use at work? Tell me in the comments.

Sources: Apache Kafka 4.4, RabbitMQ (Queues and Streams) and Amazon SQS documentation. Part 4 of 4 of the Kafka series.
